questions.stem: The process of gently heating wine, milk, and beverages to destroy pathogens without altering flavour was named after which scientist?

options.option_text: Joseph Lister (pioneer of antiseptic wound surgery)
Louis Pasteur (developed the pasteurization technique)
Robert Koch (identified pathogen causing tuberculosis)
Edward Jenner (introduced the smallpox vaccination)

questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization — heating liquids to ~60–70 °C to destroy pathogens — and the technique was named after him. Joseph Lister used carbolic acid as an antiseptic in surgery; Robert Koch identified disease-causing bacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis; neither invented pasteurization. Jenner is associated with vaccination, not heat treatment.

questions.stem: Alexander Fleming's 1928 discovery of penicillin occurred when which organism contaminated his Staphylococcus culture plates and visibly lysed the surrounding bacterial colonies?

options.option_text: Aspergillus fumigatus (a lung-infecting fungal pathogen)
Saccharomyces cerevisiae (the common baker's yeast strain)
Penicillium notatum (Fleming's contaminating blue mold)
Rhizopus stolonifer (the widespread black bread mold)

questions.explanation: Penicillium notatum (later reclassified as P. chrysogenum) contaminated Fleming's Petri dishes and secreted penicillin, which lysed the surrounding Staphylococcus colonies — the accidental observation that launched antibiotic medicine. Aspergillus and Rhizopus are molds but produce no penicillin. Saccharomyces is a baking/brewing yeast entirely unrelated to antibiotics.

questions.stem: Watson and Crick's 1953 DNA double-helix model was critically informed by which experimental technique that revealed the helical geometry and phosphate-backbone position of the molecule?

options.option_text: Density gradient centrifugation to separate DNA by mass
Electron microscopy imaging of stained chromosomal sections
X-ray crystallography data from Photo 51 (Rosalind Franklin)
Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy on purified DNA

questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography image known as Photo 51 revealed the helical shape, dimensions, and phosphate-backbone placement of DNA. Watson and Crick used this data — controversially, without her direct knowledge — to build their double-helix model. Density-gradient centrifugation (Meselson–Stahl, 1958) confirmed semi-conservative replication but revealed nothing about molecular structure.

questions.stem: Edward Jenner coined the word 'vaccine' from the Latin 'vacca' (cow). His 1796 inoculation experiment protected against smallpox using material from which disease?

options.option_text: Cowpox lesions obtained from infected dairy milkmaids
Measles scabs collected from recently recovered patients
Chickenpox pustules harvested from infected young children
Horsepox (equinia) material sourced from infected farriers

questions.explanation: Jenner observed that milkmaids who contracted cowpox did not later catch smallpox. In 1796, he inoculated James Phipps with cowpox from milkmaid Sarah Nelmes; the boy withstood subsequent smallpox exposure. 'Vaccine' derives directly from 'vacca' (cow) to honour this bovine connection. Measles, chickenpox, and horsepox played no role in Jenner's founding experiment.

questions.stem: Marconi's practical wireless telegraphy was built on the experimental work of which physicist — whose name labels the SI unit of frequency — who produced and detected radio waves in his laboratory in 1887–88?

options.option_text: James Clerk Maxwell, who predicted electromagnetic waves via equations
Heinrich Hertz, who experimentally confirmed electromagnetic radiation
Nikola Tesla, who independently patented competing US wireless systems
Oliver Lodge, who demonstrated wireless signal transmission in 1894

questions.explanation: Heinrich Hertz experimentally generated and detected radio waves in 1887–88, confirming Maxwell's theoretical predictions. The SI unit of frequency — the hertz (Hz) — is named after him, and Marconi directly adopted his antenna and spark-gap designs. Maxwell provided the mathematics but never produced radio waves experimentally. Tesla's US patents came after Marconi had already begun transmitting.

questions.stem: The Hall-Héroult process (1886), independently invented by two 22-year-old chemists on different continents, made which metal — previously rarer and more expensive than silver — commercially affordable through electrolytic smelting?

options.option_text: Titanium, which remains costly and is still refined via the Kroll process
Chromium, produced industrially by thermite reduction of chromite ore
Magnesium, extracted by electrolysis of its molten chloride compound
Aluminium, once more precious than silver and now mass-produced cheaply

questions.explanation: Before 1886, aluminium was extracted only by chemical reduction of aluminium chloride — an expensive process that made it rarer than gold. Napoleon III famously served aluminium cutlery to honoured guests while others used silver. Charles Martin Hall (USA) and Paul Héroult (France) independently discovered electrolytic reduction of alumina (Al₂O₃) dissolved in molten cryolite, slashing the price of aluminium overnight. The Kroll process applies specifically to titanium, not aluminium.

questions.stem: Which scientist first demonstrated in 1820 that electric current produces a magnetic field — the foundational discovery of electromagnetism — by observing that a live wire deflected a nearby compass needle during a lecture?

options.option_text: Michael Faraday, who demonstrated electromagnetic induction in 1831
Hans Christian Ørsted, who observed compass deflection beside a live wire
André-Marie Ampère, who mathematised the current-to-field relationship
Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, who quantified electrostatic force laws

questions.explanation: During a lecture in April 1820, Hans Christian Ørsted noticed that a current-carrying wire deflected a compass needle, proving that electricity produces magnetism — the birth of electromagnetism. Faraday discovered the reverse effect (magnetic fields inducing current) in 1831 and is therefore a common distractor. Ampère mathematically described the force between current-carrying conductors after Ørsted's discovery. Coulomb's 1780s work concerns static charge, not current-produced magnetism.
